==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|our's||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|oures}}, attested since the 1300s. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|our|s}} (compare {{m|en|-'s}}); formed by analogy to {{m|en|his}}. Displaced {{m|en|ourn}} (from Middle English {{m|enm|ouren}}) in standard speech.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref>

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈaʊəz/|/ɑːz/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈaʊɚz/|/ɑɹz/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-ours.ogg|a=US}}
* {{homophones|en|hours}}
* {{rhymes|en|aʊə(ɹ)z|ɑː(ɹ)z|s=2}}

===Pronoun===
{{head|en|pronoun|plural|ours|the possessive case of [[we]], used without a following noun|cat2=possessive pronouns|cat3=first person pronouns}}

# That or those belonging to [[us]].
## Excluding the person(s) being addressed {{q|exclusive ''ours''}}
##: {{ux|en|You can't take that! It's '''ours'''!}}
##: {{ux|en|Could we ask you to move, please. These seats are '''ours'''.}}
##: {{ux|en|This beach is a favourite of '''ours'''.|q=''[[double possessive]]''}}
## Including the person(s) being addressed {{q|inclusive ''ours''}}.
##: {{ux|en|We should ask for it back. After all, it is '''ours'''.}}
##: {{ux|en|Don't you think that '''ours''' looks much nicer than theirs?}}
# That or those belonging to any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
#: {{ux|en|French food is better than '''ours'''.}} 
# That or those belonging to people in general.
#: {{ux|en|As we get older, maintaining an active social life should be a priority of '''ours'''.|q=''[[double possessive]]''}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} That or those belonging to everyone being addressed.
#: {{ux|en|Good evening everyone. How are we all tonight? I know I've got my happy face on; have we all got '''ours''' on too?}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial|may seem patronising}} That or those belonging to an individual being addressed; {{n-g|used especially to a person in the speaker's care, or to whom advice or instruction is being given.}}
#: {{ux|en|Hello Mrs Miggins. How are we feeling this morning? Oh, what's that bottle of tablets under our chair? Is that '''ours'''?}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} {{n-g|Used to imply connection between the speaker's experiences or activities and a group of listeners}}. 
#: {{ux|en|Hey guys, in this video I'll show you how I make my upside-down sponge cake. There are lots of recipes for these, but '''ours''' is the best.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} Our house or home.
#: {{ux|en|You can stay the night at '''ours''' if you like.}}
